heading: Application for Trainee SOC Analyst
paragraphs: I am applying for the Trainee SOC Analyst role with Cyber Care in Newcastle upon Tyne. Working live customer environments on alert triage and identity administration is the way I want to learn security operations, and the structured path towards a permanent analyst position is exactly the development I am looking for.

My technical foundation comes from an MSc in Information Security at Royal Holloway, awarded with Merit, and a BCA in computer applications. I hold CompTIA Security+ and ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity. Outside of formal study I built a phishing analysis prototype that highlights suspicious email indicators and maps findings to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, evaluated against a mix of suspicious and legitimate business emails. That project is the clearest evidence I can offer of sustained self-directed interest in security operations, which your advert asks for.

In my current IT support role at The Colourful Aura I already do much of the daily work your analysts do. I manage four to five access requests a day through on-premises Active Directory, verifying business approval, granting time-limited permissions and documenting access periods and extensions. I carry out account creation, permission changes and deprovisioning with a clear audit trail. I investigate four to five suspicious emails daily, checking sender and link domains for impersonation and documenting my findings so a colleague or customer can rely on them. I am the first point of contact for 15 colleagues and use Python and PowerShell to automate repetitive checks.

Two things worth being direct about. I have not worked inside a managed detection and response service, so commercial SOC tooling and the Microsoft security stack in a customer context would be new to me. I am comfortable working to service levels and managing competing priorities, having coordinated seven or eight colleagues per shift at Co-op while handling 15 or more operational issues a week, documenting incidents and escalating unresolved risks. I am also used to recording findings methodically, which matters when someone else has to act on them.

What attracts me to TSG specifically is the employee ownership model and the emphasis on ownership as an operating standard rather than a slogan. The Ownership Ladder describes the way I already try to work: following a task through every handoff until it lands, and bringing solutions rather than problems. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Cyber Care team. Thank you for considering my application.
